races.name: Larkhall Construction Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Abando
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose German Derby form is long gone but RPR of 71 suggests he retains some ability despite poor recent efforts
runners_data.comment: Ex-German; five starts in Britain; gelded before fourth on Wednesday on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-German, beaten less than 10l in the German Derby last year; nowhere near that form in two starts for Marco Botti and similar story on his three outings for this yard; gelded before his front-running fourth of ten at Nottingham (1m2f) on Wednesday on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Curran
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will lead from the start but wind surgery and stable change raise questions about current wellbeing
runners_data.comment: Had wind op prior to his stable debut when he was tailed off at Newbury three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins when trained by Charlie Johnston; sold to join current yard for 6,000gns last October; had wind surgery prior to his stable debut when he was tailed off at Newbury (1m4f, good) three weeks ago; stepping back up in trip will be more suitable but difficult to fancy at present.

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent form with course-winning experience and top RPR of 86 making him the one to beat
runners_data.comment: Won here in April off 4lb lower; second at Ripon subsequently but finished last since
runners_data.spotlight: Scored over hurdles last November and recorded his first win on the Flat in Britain, at this track (2m1f, good to firm) in April off 4lb lower; good second at Ripon subsequently but finished last of six back there (2m, good) after slipping on the bend on the first circuit last month; swaps a visor for blinkers and may be worth forgiving latest run.

runners_data.name: Taritino
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 236 days but has course-winning form and fresh legs from recent hurdles success
runners_data.comment: Won this equivalent race two years ago when making all; must come into consideration
runners_data.spotlight: Has won twice over hurdles since his last run on the Flat last October; won this equivalent race two years ago when making all; must come into consideration.

runners_data.name: Percy Jones
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who is 0-22 on turf and was beaten 24 lengths on reappearance, making him hard to fancy
runners_data.comment: 0-22 on turf and beaten 24l on reappearance at Newbury three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins on AW at Wolverhampton; 0-22 on turf and beaten 24l on reappearance at Newbury (1m4f, good) three weeks ago; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Kotari
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner on career-low mark but was disappointing favourite last time and hasn't won for over a year
runners_data.comment: Last of six on return to action at Salisbury last month when favourite
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't won since recording a three-timer in 2024; last of six on return to action at Salisbury (1m4f, good) last month when favourite; has dropped to a career-low mark and first-time visor goes on; may be worth another chance.

runners_data.name: Golden Garden
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose only win came on all-weather and recent form suggests he's not progressing
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Goodwood last month and finished last of six subsequently at Yarmouth
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came on AW at Wolverhampton last September when trained by Jamie Osborne; flattered by his finishing position when fourth of ten at Goodwood (1m6f, good) last month and finished last of six subsequently at Yarmouth (1m6f, good); cheekpieces are introduced for the first time and needs more.

runners_data.name: Lusaka
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with two course wins but 5-pound claimer Rose Dawes takes over riding duties
runners_data.spotlight: His six wins include two over C&D; no match for No More Bolero when second here (2m1f, good to firm) in April, although he is 5lb better off with that rival; fourth of 12 at Ascot (2m, good) four weeks ago and holds place claims.

races.paceDynamic: Curran will lead uncontested from the start with No More Bolero sitting prominently behind him, creating a sustainable gallop with six hold-up horses content to settle in midfield and rear. The lack of early pressure means Curran can dictate comfortable fractions through the middle section, setting up a searching test from the home turn as the field bunches up. With most runners needing to come from off the pace, the moderate early gallop will favour those with tactical speed who can position closer to the action. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and front-runners who avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the large hold-up contingent.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Curran Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Curran maintains his lead into the straight without serious pressure
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader gets first run on the field and proves hard to peg back despite his wind surgery concerns. No More Bolero and any other prominent runners benefit from clean passages while the hold-up brigade gets caught in traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Cavalry Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is too slow and multiple hold-up horses get clear runs
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop sets up a sprint finish where the freshest finishers with the highest ratings can sweep past tiring leaders. Horses with proven turn of foot over similar distances will dominate the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: No More Bolero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero travels strongly and kicks clear approaching the furlong pole
scenarios.body: The in-form course winner uses his tactical position to slip the field when they're still organising their challenges. His recent course success and stamina prove decisive in a race that becomes a staying test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Taritino Repeats History
scenarios.trigger: If Taritino overcomes his 236-day absence to reproduce his winning tactics from two years ago
scenarios.body: The 2022 course winner's fresh legs from hurdles racing allow him to pick up the pieces when others tire in the final quarter-mile. His proven course form and making-all ability creates a surprise outcome.

watchPoints.text: Curran's breathing after wind surgery - any distress signs will signal his chance is over
No More Bolero's position through the first half-mile - needs to be handy to utilise his tactical speed
How many of the six hold-up horses get clear runs turning for home - traffic problems will be decisive
Taritino's jumping from the stalls after 236-day absence - any slow start will compromise his chances
The pace through the middle section - if too slow it will bring stamina into play and favour course specialists

races.name: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB)

runners_data.name: Bill The Bull
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner with sustainable pace style, gets uncontested lead but questionable if stamina lasts
runners_data.comment: In the frame on all three starts and is the form horse in the race.
runners_data.spotlight: Showed plenty of speed when fourth in the Brocklesby at Doncaster (5f, good) in March, and filled the same position in a Listed race at Sandown (5f, good) eight days ago; sets the standard on that form and has leading claims.

runners_data.name: Lucky Larry
runners_data.note: Newcomer with strong pedigree from Land Force, completely unknown quantity but well-bred for speed
runners_data.comment: Yard still searching for their first 2yo winner this year and may need more time.
runners_data.spotlight: First foal; by Land Force; dam placed 7f/1m AW (RPR 71), half-sister to useful 5f/6f 2yo winner Serried Ranks, out of Listed-placed 6f 2yo winner; yard still searching for their first 2yo winner this year and may need more time.

runners_data.name: South West
runners_data.note: Debutant from in-form Richard Hughes yard, breeding suggests 6f+ but could show natural ability
runners_data.comment: Yard is firing in the winners at present and worth a check in the market on this debut.
runners_data.spotlight: 12,000gns yearling; fourth foal; by Supremacy; half-brother to US winners Straight And Level (6.5f turf), Finery (1m/8.5f turf) and Brother Rice (multiple 6f dirt); dam US 5f turf winner, half-sister to Breeders Cup Dirt Mile winner Furthest Land; yard is firing in the winners at present and worth a check in the market on this debut.

runners_data.name: Texas Crown
runners_data.note: First-time out for small yard, Mayson breeding indicates speed but low-key preparation
runners_data.comment: Makes debut but yard not renowned for 2yo winners.
runners_data.spotlight: 3,000gns yearling; first foal; by Mayson; dam unraced half-sister to useful 6f winner Aplomb, out of 5f winning half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Alhebayeb; makes debut but yard not renowned for 2yo winners.

runners_data.name: Golden Oasis
runners_data.note: Oasis Dream newcomer with stamina-laden pedigree, likely needs further than 5½f
runners_data.spotlight: 4,500gns yearling; second foal; by Oasis Dream; dam unraced half-sister to winners Toro Dorado (1m-1m2f) and Uncharted (1m 2yo), out of 11.4f winning half-sister to UAE 1m2f Group 1 winner Matterhorn; could be a longer-term prospect and he's probably best watched on debut.

runners_data.name: Katie's Cavalier
runners_data.note: Hold-up style on turf debut, previous AW form suggests may prefer longer trips
runners_data.comment: Fifth on debut at Wolverhampton last month; makes turf debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth of seven on debut at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) last month; makes turf debut and may do better over longer trips.

runners_data.name: Graceful George
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner to press leader, cheekpieces added and drops back from 6f
runners_data.comment: Has shown ability in both starts to date; drops back in trip with cheekpieces added.
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown ability in both starts to date; drops back in trip with cheekpieces added and holds place claims.

runners_data.name: Madentine
runners_data.note: Slow-starting hold-up type who faded badly last time, needs to improve gate speed
runners_data.comment: Always behind after being slowly away when ninth at Kempton on her debut 16 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Always behind after being slowly away when ninth of ten at Kempton (6f, AW) on her debut 16 days ago; drops back in trip and should know more on this turf debut; not out of this.

runners_data.name: Temple Court
runners_data.note: Poor debut and gelded since, hold-up style suits but ability questions remain
runners_data.comment: Beat only one home on his debut at Newmarket three weeks ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Always behind after being slowly away when beating only one home on his debut at Newmarket (6f, good) three weeks ago; has been gelded since and drops back in trip; may have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Taseem
runners_data.note: Beaten favourite last time out, 45 days off and hard to fancy on poor form
runners_data.comment: Ran as the market suggested he would when a remote last at Yarmouth three weeks ago.
runners_data.spotlight: 80-1 outsider of six, ran as the market suggested when finishing a remote last at Yarmouth three weeks ago; gelded since; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: Modest form in better company at Newmarket, drops back in trip may not suit
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown just modest form in a couple of Newmarket novices last month; drops back in trip and may do better in time.

runners_data.name: Invincible Isaac
runners_data.note: Gelded and cheekpieces added, best form at 5f but has fading tendency in finishes
runners_data.comment: Best run when fourth on second start at Nottingham in April.
runners_data.spotlight: Best run when fourth of five on second start at Nottingham (5f, good) in April; has been gelded since his last run and cheekpieces are now added; may do better when switched to nurseries.

races.paceDynamic: Bill The Bull will take the field along as the only confirmed front runner, setting an uncontested lead in this 12-runner maiden field. With Graceful George the only prominent runner likely to press early, Bill The Bull should dictate terms through comfortable fractions over this sharp 5½f trip at Bath. The large field of hold-up horses including Katie's Cavalier, Madentine, Temple Court, Taseem, Holi Scarlett and Invincible Isaac will be relying on the pace collapsing late. This race shape strongly favours early pace and prominent runners who can secure good positions, as the wall of hold-up horses will struggle to find racing room in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Bill The Bull maintains his early speed without pressure from Graceful George
scenarios.body: The experienced front runner dictates soft fractions and has enough left to repel late challengers on this sharp track. Early pace proves decisive with hold-up horses arriving too late in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Graceful George presses Bill The Bull early and creates a genuine pace duel
scenarios.body: The two early runners burn each other out, opening the door for a well-positioned newcomer or lightly-raced type to strike late. The honest pace sets up a fair test for all running styles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of hold-up horses creates a cavalry charge in the straight
scenarios.body: Multiple runners arrive together in a messy finish where luck in running proves decisive. The pace collapses completely and it becomes a sprint from the 1f pole.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the newcomers shows significant natural ability first time out
scenarios.body: A well-bred debutant with inherent class overcomes inexperience to win going away. The race develops into a procession behind a standout performer.

watchPoints.text: Bill The Bull breaking slowly would create chaos as no other natural leader exists in this field
Graceful George applying early pressure could set up collapse for both front runners
Lucky Larry and South West market moves indicating stable confidence in debut runners
Traffic problems inevitable with 8+ hold-up horses needing room in Bath's short straight
Katie's Cavalier handling turf debut after poor AW form, surface switch could unlock improvement

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Bath City Handicap (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Mortubo
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits expected pace collapse, 38 days off seasonal return but showed promise when fourth at Lingfield on handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Kept on for fourth on seasonal/handicap debut (6f, AW) and probably still has potential
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to be placed after four starts but kept on well from the rear to take fourth on seasonal/handicap debut at Lingfield (6f, AW) in April and has plenty of scope to build on that performance; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Snow Day
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner but completely exposed as hopeless in three starts, miraculous improvement needed for handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in last place when big-priced outsider for first three runs, all over 7f on AW
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in last place when a big-priced outsider for first three races, all over 7f on AW; miraculous improvement required on this handicap/turf debut.

runners_data.name: Miss Magic Dragon
runners_data.note: Strong closer with winning C&D form last month, Pat Cosgrave booking suggests confidence after 10-day turnaround
runners_data.comment: Scored over C&D last month and both subsequent 6f runs were perfectly respectable
runners_data.spotlight: Built upon encouraging seasonal/handicap debut when beating Rogue Rebellion by a neck over C&D (good) last month; both subsequent 6f runs were perfectly respectable and the return to this track will suit; respected.

runners_data.name: Tickettothestars
runners_data.note: Proven hold-up horse with good recent form, 10 days since Lingfield second suggests trainer has specific target in mind
runners_data.comment: Big-field winner in April and 1lb ahead of the handicapper after recent Lingfield second
runners_data.spotlight: Opened account in big field at Nottingham (6f, good) in April and posted another good effort when second of 13 at Lingfield (6f, good) ten days ago; back in action before 1lb rise takes effect; likely contender.

runners_data.name: Luna Beaux
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but 133lbs top weight may anchor chances, dual AW winner stepping back up to turf
runners_data.comment: Dual AW winner this year; made the frame in higher-grade C&D race two weeks ago; a player
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 6f AW winner this year; kept on for very respectable fourth in 0-70 contest over C&D (good to firm) a fortnight ago and is 1lb lower today; probably won't be far away.

runners_data.name: Gal
runners_data.note: Prominent early but fading tendency concerning, 212 days off stable debut for Loughnane requires market support
runners_data.comment: Well down the field in three Irish maidens last year; makes stable/handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Well down the field in three Irish maidens last year (6f-7.5f); could be considered only if lively in the betting before this stable/handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Forever Glamorous
runners_data.note: Sits prominent and travels well, narrow Windsor second last month shows current form, Gina Mangan 7lb claim helps
runners_data.comment: Involved in close finishes on both starts for new stable this season (6f/5f)
runners_data.spotlight: Lost out only by a neck when second on seasonal/stable debut at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month and was also involved in a close finish when third of five at Chepstow (5f, good to soft) a fortnight ago; ought to be in the shake-up again.

runners_data.name: Geemann
runners_data.note: Front runner with concerning fade pattern, 248-day absence since poor C&D effort but recent gelding operation might help
runners_data.comment: Absent since well down the field over C&D on nursery debut in September
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed after only four starts but absent since finishing well down the field over C&D (good to firm) on nursery debut in September; gelded in May.

runners_data.name: Apex Star
runners_data.note: Prominent racer but weak finish at Salisbury turf debut nine days ago raises stamina doubts over this trip
runners_data.comment: Placed over 7f on AW last month but weakened tamely when dropped to 6f for turf debut
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race maiden; placed off 2lb higher at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) last month but weakened tamely when dropped to 6f for turf debut at Salisbury (good) nine days later and still needs to prove himself on grass.

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: Sits handy with tactical speed, good C&D second to Miss Magic Dragon last month gives confidence in conditions
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on latest outing but was close second over C&D two starts ago; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: Won on Polytrack (5f) for James Owen in January and was close second to Miss Magic Dragon over C&D (good) last month, on second start for Ronald Harris; needs to bounce back from a duff effort three weeks ago but still enters calculations.

runners_data.name: Stolen
runners_data.note: Prominent but raced too freely at Windsor, cheekpieces removed suggests trainer seeking calmer approach
runners_data.comment: Raced too freely and looked awkward ride before dropping out tamely on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Raced too freely and looked an awkward ride before dropping out tamely on recent handicap debut at Windsor (6f, good); cheekpieces removed after one use; others look much less risky.

races.paceDynamic: Geemann is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate proceedings from the outset, likely to get his own way in a sustainable rhythm early. The prominent runners Forever Glamorous, Apex Star, Rogue Rebellion, Stolen and Gal will settle just behind but won't apply serious early pressure. This creates a perfect scenario for the hold-up horses Miss Magic Dragon, Tickettothestars, Luna Beaux and Mortubo to be delivered late from off the pace. The lack of pace pressure strongly favours horses that can finish, particularly those with proven closing kicks over this course and distance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Geemann sets modest fractions without early pressure from the prominent group
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace allows the closers to wind up from ideal positions, with Miss Magic Dragon and Tickettothestars having proven C&D form to exploit these conditions. The front runners fade as the hold-up brigade sweep past in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressures Early
scenarios.trigger: If Forever Glamorous or Rogue Rebellion decide to challenge Geemann from the start
scenarios.body: The increased early tempo stretches the field and creates a more honest gallop that suits the prominent racers who can travel strongly. Forever Glamorous has the pace to sit handy and kick, while Rogue Rebellion showed good speed in his C&D second.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Geemann Sustains Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Geemann maintains his advantage and the field fails to close decisively
scenarios.body: Despite his fading tendency, the gelded son gets first run on his rivals and holds on as the closers arrive too late. His previous C&D experience and 248-day break could work in his favour if he's been freshened up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Geemann sets very slow early fractions and the field bunches up dramatically
scenarios.body: The race becomes a cavalry charge from halfway with the fastest finishers prevailing regardless of position. Tickettothestars' proven turn of foot and Miss Magic Dragon's recent C&D success make them best equipped for a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Geemann's early lead could prove unassailable if he's been transformed by gelding operation and 248-day rest
Forever Glamorous and Rogue Rebellion may apply unexpected early pressure on Geemann, changing the entire pace complexion
Miss Magic Dragon and Tickettothestars both need checking for market confidence given their proven C&D credentials
Gal requires significant market support after 212-day absence to suggest Loughnane expects improvement from Irish form
The prominent group's willingness to pressure Geemann early will determine whether hold-up horses get their ideal scenario

races.name: RUHX Handicap

runners_data.comment: Hasn't really finished off her races this year but is now 3lb below her last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Two of her six turf wins have been here, one over this distance; hasn't really finished off her races this year but is now 3lb below her last winning mark so cannot be discounted.

runners_data.spotlight: Has seven wins but has lost her form since winning here (5f, heavy) last September; has has wind surgery since her last race but has a bit to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Lazzar will break quickest and establish the early lead, with Jax Edge, Glamour Show, The Flying Seagull and Tiger Tulip all positioned prominently behind. With only one natural front-runner, Lazzar can dictate a controlled tempo without pressure, allowing the prominent runners to track comfortably. The lack of early pace pressure means this becomes a tactical affair where positioning matters more than raw speed. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses like Strike, Lequinto, Savannah Smiles and Manhattan Mirage who can exploit the lack of early gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If Lazzar sets uncontested fractions and the field bunches up
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows hold-up horses to get into perfect striking positions turning for home. Late runners with tactical speed can sweep past the tiring pace-setters in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners challenge Lazzar early creating genuine pace
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates gaps for horses with natural speed. Those tracking the pace in good positions can kick clear when others tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Lazzar's uncontested lead proves too valuable and no one can peg him back
scenarios.body: The tactical pace backfires as the leader has too much left in the tank. Lazzar's recent blinkers addition suggests connections want him more aggressive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace results in a bunched field and traffic problems in the straight
scenarios.body: Poor draws and lack of room cause interference with several horses unable to show their true ability. The race becomes a lottery won by whoever gets the clearest run.

watchPoints.text: Lazzar's blinkers could make him more aggressive than expected, potentially creating stronger pace than the single front-runner profile suggests
Strike's preference for faster ground may be compromised if the good going rides slower than ideal for his tactical style
The Flying Seagull's visor returning suggests connections want more focus, could spark improved effort after recent disappointments
Multiple hold-up horses may find themselves in traffic trouble if the controlled pace creates a bunched finish
Jax Edge's course form gives her tactical advantages but her recent failure to finish races strongly remains a concern

races.name: Mitchell & Co Classified Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Wedgewood

races.paceDynamic: Dion Baker will control this as the sole confirmed front-runner, likely getting an uncontested lead with sustainable fractions. The prominent congestion behind him featuring Wedgewood, Porfin, Rokuni, Coco Hill, and Payforanother Daay creates a traffic nightmare 2-3 furlongs out as they all want similar positions. Hold-up horses Jackie Brown, Symbol Of Hope, and Magnificent Mel will be tracking from the rear but face the challenge of weaving through the prominent pack in the straight. This race shape heavily favours the leader Dion Baker and any hold-up horse who can find clean room, as the prominent runners will compromise each other.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Baker Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Dion Baker maintains his recent front-running form and gets soft fractions
scenarios.body: The leader dictates terms unchallenged while the prominent pack battles behind, allowing Baker to kick clear when the pressure comes. His recent Brighton win proves he can sustain pace over slightly longer than this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Wedgewood or Porfin challenge Baker early and force stronger pace
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates gaps for the hold-up horses to exploit in the final furlong. Baker may crack under pressure while the patient riders benefit from the honest gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners get tangled up behind Baker in the straight
scenarios.body: The anticipated congestion materializes as five horses fight for position, leaving Baker alone in front while the others struggle for racing room. Any hold-up horse finding clear air could still threaten late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows a hold-up horse with tactical speed to sweep up from the back as the leaders tire. This suits horses who can quicken rather than those who need strong gallops.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Wedgewood or Porfin pressure Dion Baker early as this could set up the race for hold-up horses
Jackie Brown returns after 128 days with new headgear but trainer Adrian Wintle has 4 from 14 recently
Symbol Of Hope has won seven times at Bath but all from hold-up positions requiring clear runs
Traffic jam likely involving Rokuni, Coco Hill and Payforanother Daay in the prominent pack
Magnificent Mel gets 7lb from claiming jockey but was disappointing over course and distance last time

races.paceDynamic: Coast will be the lone early leader in this 9-runner field, with Addmann potentially offering some early company before fading as usual. The sustainable pace created by Coast's uncontested lead will allow the large pack of hold-up horses (Sisters In The Sky, Ken Brulee, Chiedozie, Spirited Dancer, Little Miss Magic, Port Hedland, I Was Thinking) to settle and deliver their challenges late. With no genuine speed pressure early, this race shape heavily favours closers who can produce a strong finishing kick over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Coast Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Coast gets an easy lead and maintains her rhythm throughout
scenarios.body: Coast faces no early pressure and dictates terms, making her difficult to peg back despite the wall of closers behind. Her recent improved form at Brighton suggests she can hold off late challenges when getting ideal conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sisters In The Sky Repeat
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays modest and the finish becomes a sprint
scenarios.body: Sisters In The Sky gets her perfect setup to replicate her course wins, coming from last to first in typical fashion. The even gallop allows her to unleash her proven finishing kick exactly as she did in her three Bath victories.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ken Brulee Fresh Power
scenarios.trigger: If the recently returned winner can reproduce his last-start victory
scenarios.body: Ken Brulee builds on his impressive course success 10 days ago, with the quick turnaround keeping him sharp. His proven ability at this trip and track gives him a strong chance if he's maintained his winning form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Coast stops suddenly and multiple closers arrive together
scenarios.body: Coast's lack of early pressure backfires as she dies in the final furlong, creating a blanket finish. The moderate early pace leaves too many with chances, allowing an outsider like Port Hedland or Little Miss Magic to sneak through.

watchPoints.text: Coast could dictate the entire race if allowed uncontested control of the early pace

Multiple hold-up horses may get in each other's way in the straight with limited early pace to chase
Addmann's tendency to fade late could compromise any early pace pressure on Coast

races.paceDynamic: Shirakawa will lead from the gates with Emerald Coast and Elora Prince tracking closely in the early stages. With 11 hold-up horses in the field, the early pace will be steady rather than fierce, allowing Shirakawa to dictate comfortable fractions through the first mile. The lack of genuine pace pressure means the race will develop into a sprint finish from the 2f pole, with the large pack of held-up runners all trying to make their move simultaneously. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with proven finishing kicks who can position close enough to strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Shirakawa maintains her lead without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The steady pace allows her to conserve energy and kick clear when the field comes to her, while late runners get caught in traffic. Prominent racers like Mali Star and Atalanta Mist can track the winner and pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple early leaders clashing
scenarios.body: The honest gallop sets up perfectly for the 11 hold-up horses to close with one sustained run. Mali Star and Atalanta Mist, both proven over this course and distance, can unleash powerful finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the large field bunches up approaching the final 2f with multiple runners making moves
scenarios.body: The congested finish prevents many hold-up horses from getting clear runs, allowing those positioned closer to the pace to capitalize. Emerald Coast and Elora Prince benefit from their forward positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Upset Victory
scenarios.trigger: If the main fancies fail to handle the course or distance step-up effectively
scenarios.body: An unconsidered runner who handles the unique Bath layout and finds the trip ideal can steal the prize. Ethereal Charm dropping back in trip or Maryland Star building on recent AW form could surprise.

Mali Star and Atalanta Mist both have excellent course form here and strong finishing kicks from held-up positions
Emerald Coast returns from long absence with first-time headgear and new jockey booking suggesting stable confidence
Traffic problems likely in home straight with 11 hold-up horses all looking for racing room simultaneously
Us Officer making first start in 276 days but showed ability when visored in final 2yo appearance at Chepstow

races.paceDynamic: Man Is King will take them along from the front after winning his last two by making all, with Douglas Dc likely to press him early as the only other prominent runner. This creates a steady but uncontested gallop through the middle stages, with the large hold-up contingent (Revich, Nuptown Girl, Four Fifty, City Escape, Crimson Road, Galactic Glow, Moonlit Cloud, Bobby Dassler) tracking behind in a pack. The lack of pace pressure means the leaders won't stop, but the long straight at Bath and 1m2f distance gives closers time to build momentum. This race shape clearly favours horses that can sit handy or track the pace rather than those coming from the back, as the modest early gallop will make it hard for true hold-up horses to close the gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Man Is King gets an easy lead without serious pressure from Douglas Dc early
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too slow for the hold-up brigade to make serious inroads, and Man Is King's proven front-running ability at this track sees him complete the hat-trick. His recent course wins show he handles Bath's configuration perfectly when allowed to dictate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Horses Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Douglas Dc or other prominent runners apply enough pressure to Man Is King to soften him up
scenarios.body: The pace lifts just enough to bring the race back to horses positioned close to the pace without being on the lead. Galactic Glow's excellent Bath record and Bobby Dassler's recent course form put them in ideal positions to capitalize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the middle stages creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure test of finishing speed where class and rating matter most, allowing Moonlit Cloud's superior RPR or City Escape's recent run to tell. Their hold-up styles work if the race truly becomes end-to-end.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If Man Is King and Douglas Dc engage in a sustained battle from halfway
scenarios.body: Both pace-setters weaken dramatically in the final furlong, creating opportunities for horses at bigger odds who've been tracking in behind. Nuptown Girl's AW form transferring to turf or Four Fifty finding his debut-winning form could emerge.

watchPoints.text: Man Is King could get too easy a lead if Douglas Dc doesn't press him early, making the front-runner unbeatable
Galactic Glow needs the ground to remain on the softer side of good to reproduce his best Bath form
Nuptown Girl represents the most likely surprise package if her AW form translates to turf under Rob Hornby
Four Fifty's 68-day break and tendency to fade in the finish makes him unreliable despite early promise
Bobby Dassler's recent Bath form over longer trips suggests he could outrun his odds if the pace is right
